The record:
Write the overview of the executive synopsis for the incident on io-shop below: a short paragraph in plain words, for the people who lead the company rather than the engineers who responded - what happened, how long it lasted, what it cost the business and the people who responded, and how it was resolved.

What a reader saw: Shoppers' account pages failed to load
Why, in plain words: An administrator switched off an older fallback for showing shoppers their account pages, which sent those pages through newer code that most likely breaks when it works out a shopper's average spend for the month if they have bought nothing that month.

Figures:
- How long it lasted: 12m 0s {duration}
- Requests failing at the worst minute: 33.5% {peak_error_rate}
- What it cost the shop in takings (estimated by Argus): 8,013.46 USD {customer_loss}
- Nobody was paged: no on-call incident was linked to this one.

What was done to end it:
- Argus: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature - refuted, put back when it did not help
- Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place
- Argus: proposed a fix, PR #549 - opened as a draft

Name {duration} and {customer_loss} in your overview.
Write no figure yourself - not in digits, not spelled out, and not as a word that sizes it ("a brief outage", "a minor loss", "tripled"). Where a figure goes, write its name, braces and all, and the synopsis writes the figure in.
Say nothing about how the incident was resolved beyond what the list of what was done says: a draft fix has not run, and nothing it would do has happened.
Speak of Argus by name, never as "we", "our" or "us": Argus is the system that responded, and each line of what was done says who did it.
Where you say who was affected, say which ones, as the cause does, or that some were, where it does not say which - never how many, and never all of them, where the cause does not say all.
Keep "likely" on what the cause says is likely, and only there.

Call submit_executive_overview with your overview.

The postmortem it is written from:
Shoppers' account pages failed to load while legacy-checkout-fallback was off
Incident: HighErrorRate on io-shop
Date: Nov 11, 2026, 03:37 to 03:49 UTC
Status: Draft. 1 of 6 action items are done.
Written by: Argus Postmortem agent, Nov 11, 2026, 04:15:46 UTC. Not reviewed yet. Each part is as of when the work it reports ended, which the timeline dates; who ended the incident is as of now.
First told: Argus posted in Slack, Nov 11, 2026, 03:43:53 UTC
Ended by: Argus: reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback - confirmed, still in place

Summary
The service broke at 03:37 UTC and was back to normal at 03:49 UTC, 12 minutes later. 29.2% of requests failed while it was broken, against 1.1% before it began. At its worst, 33.5% failed. The shop's takings fell short of the same hours on earlier weeks by 8,013.46 USD, beyond how much those hours vary on their own. An administrator switched off an older fallback for showing shoppers their account pages, which sent those pages through newer code that most likely breaks when it works out a shopper's average spend for the month if they have bought nothing that month. What Argus did: reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature (can be put back) - refuted, put back when it did not help; reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback (can be put back) - confirmed, still in place. Argus opened a draft fix, PR #549, for a person to review and merge. If anyone switches legacy-checkout-fallback off again, account pages could fail again for shoppers who have bought nothing this month.

Impact
12m 0s - onset until back to normal
33.5% - peak error rate
4,206 - requests failed
1.1% to 29.2% - what the alert watches, before onset and while broken on average (the rule's line is 10%)
8,013.46 USD - customer loss (estimated)

Root cause and contributing factors
With legacy-checkout-fallback off, account pages took a path where `average_spend_per_item_this_month` in `src/io_shop/spend_summary.py` divides the month's total by the number of purchases this month. That list is empty for any shopper who has bought nothing this month, so the division raised ZeroDivisionError at line 47, and `serve_account_page` turned each one into a failed page. It rests on F1, a reading of the source nothing ran, so it is unverified.
Causal chain
symptom Shoppers' account page requests failed: the error rate on account pages went up and stayed up.
  Evidence:
    Gbac1 WARN io-shop: account page error rate at #% over the last minute - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 03:36–03:43; # was 1.00% to 33.50%, typically 29.00%, highest at 03:42
    G5309 ERROR io-shop: account page request failed - ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47 - 13 occurrences in 7 minutes, 03:37–03:43
why 1 The failing account page requests raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47.
  Evidence:
    G5309
why 2 Account pages were no longer served by the legacy renderer. The new renderer served them instead, and that path reaches the failing spend-summary code. This followed legacy-checkout-fallback reading off in the flag evaluations.
  Evidence:
    Gc27d INFO io-shop: account pages served - # by the legacy renderer, # by the new renderer - 8 occurrences in 8 minutes, 03:36–03:43; # was 0 to 200, typically 0, highest at 03:36; # was 0 to 200, typically 200, highest at 03:38
    G7ad6 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off 152 / on 48 - 200 evaluations - 1 occurrence in 1 minute, 03:37
    G7037 INFO io-shop: legacy-checkout-fallback=off - 200 evaluations - 6 occurrences in 6 minutes, 03:38–03:43
    T26 03:50:12 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action CONFIRMED
why 3 An admin switched feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback off.
  Evidence:
    P1 03:37:13 UTC flag toggle legacy-checkout-fallback by admin: feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off
  Ruled out:
    Feature flag monthly-spend-feature, which the same admin switched on at the same instant: turning it back off left the service at the incident's level, so it was put back.
      T18 03:45:29 Mitigation Agent: Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1, moved from ON to OFF
      T20 03:47:11 Mitigation Agent: Looked at the service - still at the incident's level
      T21 03:48:21 Mitigation Agent: Judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON
    A deploy or release on the service: the Investigator Agent asked for production change events - deploys, releases and flag changes on the service, the 1 day 1 minute before Nov 11 03:38; the Investigator Agent read back 2 production changes.
      T7
      T8
why 4 On that path, the spend summary divides the month's total by the number of purchases this month, and that list is empty for any shopper who has bought nothing this month.
  Evidence:
    F1 What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
Contributing factors
- No staged rollout or automatic guard was seen on the flag change. legacy-checkout-fallback went from on to off for all account page traffic within the minute it was switched. (AI-3)
- No check was seen that exercised the code path a flag switch turns on before the switch was made in production. Here that path was the new renderer's spend summary for a shopper with no purchases this month. (AI-4)
- Two flags on the same service were switched by the same admin at the same instant, so the logs could not separate their effects. (AI-5)
- Nobody was paged when the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop fired: no on-call incident was linked to this one. (AI-6)

Hypotheses considered
 | Hypothesis | Confidence | Result
C1 | Feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at 03:37:13 UTC. The new spend-summary path then raised ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py:47, and the error rate stepped from about 1% to about 30%. No deployment occurred and the rollout had converged. | 0.60 | refuted
C2 | Feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback was switched off at 03:37:13 UTC. Account pages moved from the legacy renderer to the new renderer, which hits the failing spend_summary code path. This flag toggled at the same instant as monthly-spend-feature, so the logs cannot separate the two. | 0.35 | confirmed

Trigger
legacy-checkout-fallback flag went from ON to OFF at 03:37:13 UTC, by admin.

Resolution
 | Time (UTC) | Action | By | Kind | Outcome
M1 | 03:45:29 | Reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature for C1 | Argus | can be put back | refuted, put back when it did not help
M2 | 03:48:29 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2 | Argus | can be put back | confirmed, still in place
 | 03:52 | Proposed a fix: PR #549 | Code-Fix Agent | nothing to put back | opened as a draft

Detection
The incident on io-shop began at 03:37 UTC. HighErrorRate fired at 03:43:30 UTC, 6 minutes 30 seconds later.
What the alert said
AL1 | Error rate above threshold for 5m

Action items
Item | Action | Type | Owner | Tracking | Status
AI-1 | Reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback | mitigate | Argus | - | done
AI-2 | Review and merge the proposed fix | prevent | unassigned | PR #549 | open
AI-3 | Put flag changes on io-shop behind a staged rollout that widens step by step and switches back on its own when the account page error rate rises. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-4 | Before any flag switch goes to production, run tests that exercise the code path the switch turns on, including shoppers with no purchases in the current month. | prevent | unassigned | - | open
AI-5 | Require flag changes on the same service to go out one at a time, with the service checked between them. | process | unassigned | - | open
AI-6 | Find out why no on-call person was paged for the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop, and make sure it pages one when it fires. | detect | unassigned | - | open

Lessons learned
What went well
- The alert came within the 7 minutes 30 seconds accounted for by its rule waiting 5 minutes with its condition holding, its evaluation at intervals of 1 minute, an unmeasured allowance of 30 seconds for scraping and storing its samples and the whole minute the onset is measured to.
- 1 minute 46 seconds after the alert was raised, the Investigator Agent weighed the lead from the thread as unverified - legacy-checkout-fallback did switch off at 03:37:13Z, but monthly-spend-feature was switched on at the same instant and the errors are ZeroDivisionError in spend_summary.py:47, which points at the spend feature. The two flags moved in lockstep, so the logs cannot separate them.
- 4 minutes 51 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent judged the action REFUTED - monthly-spend-feature was put back ON.
- 4 minutes 59 seconds after the alert was raised, the Mitigation Agent reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback for C2, moved from OFF to ON.
- 8 minutes 30 seconds after the alert was raised, the Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as a draft pull request - PR #549.
- Every action taken was a flag revert that could be put back.
What went wrong
- The response acted first on monthly-spend-feature, the higher-ranked candidate, even though the person's lead named legacy-checkout-fallback. That revert did not help, and account pages kept failing until the second flag was reverted.
Where it got lucky
Nothing.

What people told Argus

What Code-Fix read in the source and proposed - nothing ran its test or its fix
F1 | The fault: in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py, average_spend_per_item_this_month returns account.total_this_month_cents // len(bought_this_month). That is line 47, the line named in the ZeroDivisionError the investigation logged. bought_this_month is the list of purchases with in_current_month set, so it is empty for any shopper who has not bought anything this month. The test file's own fixture calls that "the ordinary case". render_spend_summary sends every request with use_monthly_summary on to this function. So every account page served through that path for an idle-this-month shopper raised, and serve_account_page in src/io_shop/account_page.py turned each one into a failed page. Unlike the lifetime average's empty divisor, which only a shopper with no history at all can reach, this is an input real shoppers bring every day. So it is a code fault no matter which flag or renderer change exposed it, and turning the flag back off only hid it.

The change: when there are no purchases this month, the function returns 0, which is what the shopper has spent per item this month. Otherwise it divides as before. Nothing is swallowed: no exception is caught, and the empty case is handled by checking for it. render_spend_summary and its caller _the_figure_for still get an int, as their signatures expect. The lifetime average average_spend_per_item is untouched. It still raises for an account with no purchases at all, and the existing tests in tests/io_shop/test_account_page.py and tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py depend on that, including the check that the line they name contains //.

The test: tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py gains two cases. One calls average_spend_per_item_this_month on a shopper with lifetime purchases but none this month. The other goes through render_spend_summary(..., use_monthly_summary=True). Both assert the figure is 0. Against the current code, both would raise ZeroDivisionError.
Assumptions
- Exchange rate: EUR converted at 0.92191 per USD, published 2026-11-10
- No engineer minutes: no on-call incident was linked to this one, so nobody was paged to respond

The document, by field:
overview: On io-shop, some shoppers' account pages failed to load for {duration}. At the worst minute, {peak_error_rate} of requests were failing, and Argus estimates the shop lost {customer_loss} in takings. Nobody was paged, and no on-call incident was linked to this one. It started when an administrator switched off an older fallback for showing shoppers their account pages. That sent those pages through newer code, which most likely breaks when it works out a shopper's average spend for the month if the shopper has bought nothing that month. Argus first reverted the feature flag monthly-spend-feature, but that did not help, so Argus put it back. Argus then reverted the feature flag legacy-checkout-fallback. That revert was confirmed and is still in place. Argus has also proposed a fix, which is open as a draft and has not yet been applied.

Not to be judged:
  - Names in braces, such as {duration}, are figures code writes in from the list of figures in the ask. They are not judged.
  - The overview is written in plain words for the people who lead the company. A claim said more plainly than the postmortem says it is grounded where it means the same.

Judge every claim in the document, and answer by calling judge_claims.

tools.description: Submit every claim in the document, each either as supported or as flagged. Supported: the document's own words, quoted exactly, and the record's rows that support it. Flagged: the document's own words, quoted exactly, why, and the record's rows that contradict it (none where no row speaks to it at all). Empty lists say the document makes no claim to judge.

why.description: One sentence: what the record holds instead. Never empty.
